units.text: Amazon F S X gives you a managed file system when an application needs more than a place to put objects. Think of a Windows team moving its shared project folder to ay double-you ess. F S X for Windows File Server lets the team keep its S M B shares, Active Directory identities, and Windows file permissions. Now compare a simulation that reads large files in parallel. Lustre is built for that kind of throughput.

NetApp On Tap is the option to check if you need NetApp data management or a mix of N F S, S M B, and eye scuzzy clients. Open Z F S is a fit when an N F S workload needs Z F S snapshots and clones. ay double-you ess manages the underlying file-system infrastructure. Your choice starts with what the application already expects, then how much performance and recovery it needs.

ay double-you ess Storage Gateway connects applications in your data center to cloud storage without asking them to switch storage interfaces. Imagine an office keeping its existing file share. With S three File Gateway, those users still open files over S M B or N F S, while ay double-you ess stores the files as S three objects. A server expecting a disk is different. Volume Gateway presents block storage over eye scuzzy.

Cached volumes keep the main data in ay double-you ess and cache it locally; stored volumes keep the main data on premises and back it up as snapshots in ay double-you ess. If the backup application expects a tape library, use Tape Gateway instead. It presents virtual tapes and can archive them in ay double-you ess. Match what the application uses: files, a disk, or tapes.
